subject.title: fix(cli): bound model run image reads with per-file and aggregate budget

question: Should model-run image ingestion guarantee prompt rejection of non-regular input paths on Windows, rather than accepting an ordinary open that may block before descriptor validation?
rationale: Node’s POSIX nonblocking flag does not provide the required Windows behavior, so maintainers need to choose the supported Windows security/availability contract before accepting a platform-specific regression.

options.title: Implement a Windows-safe acquisition path
options.body: Use a reviewed Windows primitive or a narrowly safe design that rejects non-regular input without allowing the CLI to wait indefinitely, and add focused proof.

options.title: Accept the documented limitation
options.body: Explicitly accept that adversarial Windows non-regular paths may block, with a maintainer-approved supported-platform statement and user-facing documentation.

options.title: Limit the change to proven platforms
options.body: Preserve the current Windows acquisition behavior and apply the descriptor-bound nonblocking change only where its safety contract is established.

recommendation.title: Implement a Windows-safe acquisition path
recommendation.body: Use a reviewed Windows primitive or a narrowly safe design that rejects non-regular input without allowing the CLI to wait indefinitely, and add focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the final platform-boundary and nonblocking-acquisition commits, making them the closest available routing candidate for the technical tradeoff.
